pieces.text: The fix is not discipline. Write down when it was last done.

alt: A table of four maintenance jobs with how often each is due and what a skipped one turns into, beside a note about writing down the last done date.
caption: Four of the eight jobs from the guide, with how often each is due and what skipping it leads to.

alt: Two cards comparing service intervals: heating and water jobs on one side, safety and roof jobs on the other, each with how often it is due.
caption: Typical intervals from the guide. Your own manual wins over any table.

alt: A blank one-page appliance record with five fields: make and model, serial number, install date, warranty end and last service.
caption: The five fields to write while the appliance is in front of you.

items: Ask who holds the alarm code

pieces.text: Read the survey again as a to-do list, and give every timescale a date.

alt: A day-one checklist for a new house covering meter photos, shutoffs, suppliers, alarm code and alarm tests, with a note about rereading the survey.
caption: The day-one list from the guide, to do while the previous owner is still reachable.

pieces.eyebrow: Jobs that belong to a season

steps.what: Drain outdoor taps and irrigation lines
Service cooling, inspect roof, clear gutters

alt: A four-step seasonal timeline: drain taps before the freeze, gutters and heating in autumn, cooling and roof in spring, exterior work in summer.
caption: The jobs that really belong to a season. Everything else runs on an interval.

pieces.eyebrow: Write these down the same day
items: Who came and what it cost

alt: A checklist of what to write after a home repair: the symptom, the diagnosis, the part replaced, what to watch for next, and who came.
caption: What to record before the technician drives away, besides the invoice.

pieces.eyebrow: Before you pay for a repair
pieces.question: Before you pay for a repair, check:
options: Do you have proof of purchase?
Do you have the serial number?

pieces.text: With some brands, registering extends a warranty and brings recall notices.

alt: A card asking what to check before paying for a repair, listing warranty status, the annual service record, proof of purchase and serial number.
caption: The four things that most often sink a warranty claim, per the guide.

pieces.text: Where you cannot find out when it was last done, assume it is due.

alt: A table of typical service lives for boiler, water heater, air conditioning and roof, beside a note to treat unknown service dates as due.
caption: Typical service lives from the guide. Your own equipment may differ.

pieces.text: Photograph the whole plate rather than choosing which code to copy.

alt: A table of where the data plate sits on a fridge, washing machine, dishwasher and water heater, beside a note to photograph the whole plate.
caption: Four of the ten appliances covered in the guide, and where each keeps its plate.

pieces.eyebrow: The fall list, month by month

steps.what: Book the heating tune-up, seal entry gaps
Drain outdoor faucet, blow out irrigation
Clear gutters once the leaves are down

alt: A three-step fall timeline: book the heating tune-up and seal gaps in September, drain the faucet in October, clear gutters in November.
caption: Fall in three months, using the jobs from the guide.

pieces.text: The first freeze is the deadline, not a date on the calendar.

alt: A five-item winterizing checklist covering the outdoor faucet, irrigation, window air conditioner, humidifier pad and entry points, with a note on the freeze deadline.
caption: The five winterizing jobs from the guide.

alt: A blank home maintenance log page with fields for the date, what was done, who did it, what it cost and one note for next time.
caption: The four fields and one note the guide says a log needs.

pieces.caption: Default for a normal one inch filter
pieces.foot: Sooner with pets, dust or allergies

alt: A card showing three months as the default furnace filter interval, beside a checklist of the size and location facts to write down once.
caption: The default interval and the facts to note, from the guide.

pieces.text: Note which way it turns and any tool it needs.

alt: Two cards comparing a wheel handle gate valve with a lever handle ball valve, beside a note to write down which way it turns.
caption: How to tell the two common main shutoff valve types apart.

alt: Two cards comparing what goes in a home binder, such as shutoff locations and contacts, with what never does, such as passwords and alarm codes.
caption: Write where things are and who to call, never the codes themselves.

pieces.text: Report in writing and keep a copy, so the message carries a date.

alt: A table of four day-one rental records: photos, lease dates, deposit and what you reported, beside a note to report in writing.
caption: The four records from the guide. Not legal advice; rules vary by place.
